newsitem.title: UK: Semtex traces found in London taxis, airports.
newsitem.headline: Semtex traces found in London taxis, airports.

text.p: Scientists trying to find out if innocent people could be exposed to illegal explosives found traces of them in the backs of London taxis and airport luggage handling areas, New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
Some forensic experts said the surprising findings meant that some people innocent of wrongdoing could be contaminated by the traces and perhaps even convicted of a crime.

The scientists at the Defence Evaluation Research Agency mostly tested police cars and found measurable traces of either Semtex or nitroglycerin in eight out of 21, while more than half of police stations tested were contaminated.
It was likely the chemicals came off the clothes of bomb squad officers, they said.
They also looked at taxis based at Heathrow airport and found two out of 20 had traces of RDX, a chemical constituent of Semtex. RDX was also found in the baggage handling area of Gatwick airport.
The magazine said forensic experts disagreed on whether this meant people could get traces of the chemicals on their clothes innocently.
"What is required is a much bigger survey," said Brian Caddy of the University of Strathclyde.
The magazine said police stations were making more efforts to clean up since the survey was done.
